For q-49439, the power rule gives (4/11)(x-100)^(11/4)+C, equivalent to the selected fourth root for x>=100. The q-12498 and q-49439 prose incorrectly says the final answer is written in terms of u; their displayed final answers correctly use x. For q-43308, the product becomes (1-sin²θ)/sinθ=cosθ cotθ. For q-65218, sin x csc x=1 reduces the expression to 2(1-cos²x)=2sin²x. For q-23526, combining numerators gives (1-cos²θ)/sinθ=sinθ. For q-1583, sec²A-tan²A=1. For q-119864, factoring 1-sin²x and canceling against sin x-1 gives -(1+sin x). For q-65182, factoring sin²x gives 1/(1+cos x), so f(x)=1+cos x. These trigonometric equalities retain the original expressions' domain restrictions. For q-31600, L'Hopital's rule gives (ln(x+2)+x/(x+2))/(2x+3), whose limit at -1 is -1. For q-72333, L'Hopital's rule gives -x/e^(1/x), tending to 0 from the right. For q-72336, multiplying numerator and denominator by x^4 gives x²/(1-x^4), tending to 0. For q-31517, two applications of L'Hopital's rule give 1/(xe^x), tending to 0. For q-49453 and q-15707, shifted logarithmic antiderivatives have coefficients 3 and 2 respectively. For q-72446, substitution gives -(1/2)ln|5-2x|+C; writing C=-(1/2)ln K, with K>0, gives the selected logarithm. Every positive K corresponds to an arbitrary real integration constant.",
